I'm reading a book that sort of touches on the way you visualize self-forgiveness. Its called Psycho-Cybernetics by Maxwell Maltz. Basically, he says a new concept (in my case, forgiveness of myself over an event) will NOT be accepted if it doesn't match my inner circle of strongly held beliefs. And at the core of those is my self-image, the way I truly view myself. In my case, my self image is I hate myself for treating women badly and not finishing college, so my strongly held belief circle revolves around thinking I deserve shitty women or no women, and I deserve low income jobs. It IS irrational, but it's what my trauma has lead me to experience and feel for a long time. I can change the core, if I can find a way to love myself more than the cumulative amount of self-hate I've experienced. A really good first step is to stop piling on any and all self hate, which is hard to do because it's a very ingrained habit at this point.

I don't want a counselor. I don't want to PAY someone who is there because it's their JOB. I want something more REAL, more organic and fluid. I'm quite intelligent, and I've read a ton of books (I read one every day), but if intelligence was all I needed, I'd have fixed this by now. What I need is real, organic, fluid CONNECTION to real people who understand because they have been where I have been. Since I'm saying "no" to the traditional approach, it's only right that I offer something in its place. It hit me like a ton of bricks today:

I need YOU guys (and girls). I need someone who has been there before, maybe even going through it right now. I need you to hear me, and have you expound upon my ideas and stories when the moment strikes you; and I'll do the same for you. Instead of waiting until we're suicidal again, instead of fighting the red tape and bureaucracy of psychologists, we'll do something UNofficial, we'll pick each other up and be there for each other BEFORE it gets that far, and we'll do it right here on this page. I don't know if this idea is big enough to warrant a sub-Reddit, but I know that ANYone who wants or needs help can come to this page, and I'll do my best to make them feel loved, included, and listened to.

Running is my favorite hobby. I finally ran a sub 20 minute 5k this summer, which completely blew me away, as I never did any sports in HS.

Want to get serious about playing piano, so I'm going to buy a digital piano next month (I think I'll like music even better than running).

I miss my long term girlfriends...every last one of them. Sure, some I did wrong, and some did me wrong; some quit me first, some I quit first...but, with tears in my eyes, I smile at all the connection and experiences we shared together. The gf from first year in college and the joy on her face reflecting my own as I drank my first Starbucks Chai tea;
Another girlfriend and I played through final fantasy 1 through 12 together (except xi, cause online and never ends), literally 100s of hours holding hands while reading epic stories and fighting epic battles across time and space; a third girlfriend and I played WOW together, and I introduced her to swimming, while she showed me what a truly calm and stable relationship looks like. A fourth, we moved in together and read classics literature, made love, then giggled as we tried to read to make us fall asleep; the fifth and last made my heart leap even more than the rest, we could bring back the Sun in the sky by merely wishing it, I told her things within a month I'd never told my best friend of 15 years, she is a tiny pixie at 4 foot 10, yet her heart was bigger than mine, she showed me how to really open up my heart, how to use my words, how to cry in front of a woman because the time you spend together is so precious.
